result: I found and modelled disorder in the water region, and the data support it. In the original model, water O20 had an extreme displacement parameter (Ueq 0.30 Å², with the ellipsoid about 42 times longer in one direction than another). Two difference-map peaks sat about 0.7 Å either side of it, and there was an unexplained 6.2 e/Å³ peak about 2.1 Å from O22. I split O20 into two sites, O20A and O20B, with occupancies tied to one free variable. The distances then showed how the waters pair up. O22 is only 2.32 Å from O20B, so the two can't both be present, and O22 belongs with O20A. The 6.2 peak is 2.03 Å from O20A but a reasonable 2.76 Å from O20B, so I added it as a new water, O26, alongside O20B. That gives PART 1 = O20A + O22 and PART 2 = O20B + O26, refining to 0.54 : 0.46. R1 fell from 0.0285 to 0.0230, wR2 from 0.085 to 0.065 and GooF from 1.47 to 1.12, with one fewer parameter. All four disordered oxygens now have sensible isotropic displacement parameters (0.03–0.045 Å²). The remaining difference peaks, at most 3.0 e/Å³, are ripples about 0.8 Å from the Ta atoms, not missing atoms. The rest of the structure is ordered and I left it unchanged.
